notes.title: Important update (1.0.22.1)
notes.notes:
“Skip disturbing scenes” toggle was added in a previous update. Considering sensitive time we’re living in, we can do better than that. You deserve better. All scenes alluding to self harm are now completely removed from the game. These scenes have no place in superhot virtual reality. We regret it took us so long.

We’re commited to shipping this update to all vr platforms.

-superhot team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR 1.0.16 patch
notes.notes:
Hello all!

Speedrunning our way to the end of the year, we bring you a patch filled with fixes and upgrades, a huge chunk of them being community reported ones!

The one you might find the most interesting is that [b]Mindwave has been overhauled, revised and simplified.[/b] Now it aims better, should always work without failure and you only need to hold both triggers, though clenching whole fist will still work so that’s obviously the fancier way to blow your foes’ brains!

Considering game flow, [b]now after each launch you’ll find yourself in the Hacker Room[/b] which will serve as your general gateway into delicious, violent, escapist reality of SUPERHOT VR. After putting your in-game, white VR headset on you’ll get to the level you have stopped at when you finished your last game session.

Speaking of [b]the in-game headset[/b], it [b]should be easier to reach from now on[/b]. You can still just grab it in a realistic manner, but should you need it, a bit “force pull” is available to you as well. And after you get into the simulation you shouldn’t spot any case of thrown objects bouncing off the enemies; if you throw it properly, you’ll end the foe rightly for sure. Some of you made us aware of this issue and rightly so!

There’s also a number of smaller fixes that would not make for a nice read. Once again, your help in finding bugs, your reports and cooperation (you’re sending us videos of bugs and it’s just brilliant!) and your feedback allowed us to perfect SUPERHOT VR a little bit more. Thank you so much!


[b]SUPERHOT VR 1.0.16 patch changelog:[/b]
— Mindwave overhauled and made easy to use
— Improved Hacker Room’s role as the game hub during story progression
— Made the in-game headset easier to reach
— Ensured that thrown objects will prove harder than the enemies
— Small localisation (language-related) fixes
— Hardcore mode revamped
— Dozens of minor bug fixes, including the one that raises defensive value of a refrigerator. Yes, I’m serious.

Thank you for being with us!
Paweł from SUPERHOT

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.14
notes.notes:
Hey There

This is going to be a nifty update.
For past few weeks, our porting super squad has been working hard on bringing SUPERHOT VR to new VR headset, Valve Index. It’s a great headset on its own but what really stands out are its Knuckle controllers.
With the support of those bad boys, SUPERHOT VR will be able to track each finger independently for more realistic and nuanced recreation of your hands.
This, in turn, will lend itself nicely to even better in-game immersion.
Which means that you will be able to do stuff like:

[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/772846378245516789/B4FB32FA0828D496ADECF0FDC167799CEB92E447/[/img]

Or something like that:
[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/772846378245520659/CE147693B95D6237E239EB37BFF24E4ADD63EA76/[/img]

Maybe this too:
[img]https://steamuserimages-a.akamaihd.net/ugc/772846378245528365/3C43378713D38F502EB77DFFC36B6F6797965133/[/img]

Except for the Valve Index support we've fixed and improved a few things for your Virtual Reality convenience:

[list]
[*]  Recentering option has been brought back to Oculus headsets 
([url=https://support.oculus.com/200305533724698/]instruction here[/url]) 
[*] Haptic rumble works again on all controllers.
[*] Added a slight hint during “Aim for the head” scene.
[/list]

Our bugfixing victories this time: 
[list]
[*] Fixed particles bug.
[*] Fixed small graphics' errors on lightmaps.
[*] Small yet essential language fixes.
[*] Other tiny, itsy, bitsy bugs that we ruthlessly smushed for your comfort.
[/list]


Let us know what you think about the update. Oh, and if you get yourself an Index, please show us them skills. I personally would love to see how people will use those new controllers.

Drink lots of water,
Szymon from SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.13
notes.notes:
Hey There

Past weeks have been quite busy for us.
We’ve released [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/617830/announcements/detail/1651042686388981889]SUPERHOT VR: Arcade Edition[/url], SUPERHOT VR launched on [url=https://www.oculus.com/experiences/quest/1921533091289407/]Oculus Quest[/url] and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/690040/announcements/detail/1601504362738840354]SUPERHOT: MIND CONTROL DELETE[/url]  got it’s sexy new update.
Pfffew.

That didn’t stop us from doing a bit of update work on SUPERHOT VR.

[b]Let’s see what’s new:[/b]

[list]
[*] Liv integration(HTC Vive headsets only) - Now you will be able to do cool mixed-reality gameplay yourself. Something like [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jT11OEiA9x4]this[/url] for example.

[*] Rift S support - It works, it’s fine and dandy. Go and play SUPERHOT VR without external tracking sensors. Watch them walls though.

[*] Localisation QA - The game went through a detailed localisation QA process. Minor language bugs were killed without mercy. Achievements finally got translated as well. Yay.
[/list]

That’s it Ladies and Gents
Have a good day.

Cheers
Szymon from SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.12
notes.notes:
Hey There

Here is a tiny patch for an annoying bug.
Few Oculus users reported issues with gripping objects in SUPERHOT VR.
To tackle that we made a slight change in the controller gripping threshold. It should work fine now.

Thanks for being diligent and letting us know about that issue!

Cheers
Szymon from SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.10
notes.notes:
Hey there,

How is your virtual life going? 
There were a few games issues that needed to be fixed.

[list]
[*] [b]Oculus SDK support for Oculus users[/b]

That's it! Let us know what you think about the changes.

Cheers,
Szymon form SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.5/1.0.6 (bug fix)
notes.notes:
[EDIT]
Fixed the fix. There was a bug in the demo where it used one control scheme in one level and then switched to other scheme. This was probably causing other issues.

Hey everybody,

We know you've all been waiting for this. The new patch is here, and it contains are as follows:

[list]
    [*]Fixed a bug where the items were falling out of non-dominant hand in Oculus version
    [*]General optimization
    [*]Some minor bug tweaks
    [*]New feature - we added a demo/party mode. Basically first level of the game looped, ideal for showing the game to friends at parties or running on events and arcades.
[/list]

After clicking play button in Steam you can choose between normal version and demo mode. Demo will restart automatically after 5 seconds from displaying "You can now safely remove your headset" info.

That's it for today! Let us know what you think about the demo mode :)

Cheers,
Sandra form SUPERHOT TEAM

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.3 - new control scheme goes default + a little extra
notes.notes:
Alrighty! So we spent the last few days testing and retesting the new control scheme and had you guys check it out as well. It does seem to be more comfortable for most, so we're now pushing the update to the default channel.

Quick refresher on what this actually means (and what we totally look like in skintight spandex):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9UGFOzrIlKg

To sum it up:
[list]
[*]To grab an object use the trigger
[*]To release it use the touchpad
[*]You grabbed a gun? Shoot with the trigger.
[*]Wanna go melee? Just hold the trigger while unarmed and punch away!
[/list]


So the complete, thoroughly documented change log for the 1.0.3 patch shapes up to:
[list]
    [*] New control scheme
    [*] Changed pivots on some objects to make them more comfortable
    [*] Updated ingame animated tutorial 
    [*] Moved some objects around a bit
    [*] Fixed some performance issues
[/list]

And if you're already used to the original control scheme and would rather have it stay that way, we've got a special beta branch just for you. Follow these three steps and squish away on the Vive grip buttons just as you did before: 
[olist]
    [*] In your Steam library, right click on SUPERHOT VR and click on "Properties"
    [*] Click on the BETAS tab
    [*] Change the drop down to "original-vive-control-scheme".
[/olist]



PS. In case you haven't been watching the Sony E3 conference last night, I'm guest-posting for Szymon while he's out at E3 announcing SUPERHOT + SUPERHOT VR for PS4 🔥.  Here's a super fancy new trailer for that:
https://youtu.be/Sg5xLLeYimc


Cheers!
Tom from SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR Patch 1.0.2 (test branch)
notes.notes:
Hey there!

A new day, a new patch.

Here is a little summary :
[list]
[*]New control scheme
[*]Changed pivots on objects
[*]Updated ingame animated tutorial 
[*]Fixed some performance issues
[/list]

First and foremost we decided to tackle the issue of controls.
Previous setup wasn't all that comfortable to some people and we are all about your comfort :)
We want to test this new control scheme and gather your feedback.
For now it will be available only on "Alternative-vive-control-scheme".

How to access this test branch:
[list]
[*]In your Steam library, right click on SUPERHOT VR and click on "Properties"
[*]Click on the BETAS tab
[*]Change the drop down to "Alternative-vive-control-scheme".
[/list]

So here is a little intro video to the new control scheme.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9UGFOzrIlKg&feature=youtu.be

Easy right?

To sum it up:
[list]
[*]To grab an object use the trigger
[*]To release it use the touchpad
[*]You grabbed a gun? Shoot with the trigger.
[*]Wanna go melee? Just hold the trigger while unarmed and punch away!
[/list]


That's it for today! Let us know what you think about new controls.

Cheers
Szymon form SUPERHOT Team

notes.title: SUPERHOT VR happy launch weekend and patch 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

It's been one wild exciting week for us. We just came back from Digital Dragons, bringing home two awesome golden dragon egg awards for Best Design and Best VR Game. They're super heavy. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28859394/be40acbaec9e383cead9e9e42fe5668cc6884016.jpg[/img]



Slawek, the Vive dev, has been hard at work crunching at bugs you guys reported since the release two days ago. We've got a first batch of them fixed and there's a patch rolling out right now. The biggest bits that we've resolved:

[b]Changelist for SUPERHOT VR 1.0.1 - 27 May 2017[/b]
[list]
[*] Solved issues with hand-controller position mapping for some players
[*] Improved progress reset thingy (saw issues with restarting the story)
[*] Changed how some items are gripped (certain items stick to hands more naturally)
[*] Fixed seldom crashes with our VR stats system
[*] Performance and rendering quality improvements
[/list]

We're combing through all the feedback and forums, so definitely poke us here or send an email to ifoundabug@superhotgame.com if you see anything else you'd like us to fix. 🐞



Plus there's a bunch of us now at Pixel Heaven, showing SUPERHOT VR and rooting for SUPERHOTs nomination for the Pixel.Awards. Keep fingers crossed guys! 

Thank you for being awesome! 
<3 Tom


Odi the SUPERHOTDOG 💖s you too. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28859394/03d82264a5f1191ee9a9a36c2bcee70c991f1fb1.jpg[/img]
